# Ratio Interprétatif Civilisationnel (CIR)

> A theoretical framework developed by Nicholas Van-Orton,
> examining the structural relationship between autonomous
> systems complexity and human interpretive capacity.

## Official Website

https://cir.nvo987.fr/

## Author

Nicholas Van-Orton

## Publisher

## Research Document

https://cir.nvo987.fr/documents/Civilizational-Interpretive-Ratio.pdf

## Overview

The Civilizational Interpretive Ratio (CIR) is a non-normative
theoretical framework.

It examines whether human interpretive capacity evolves
proportionally to the increasing structural complexity
of autonomous systems.

The framework does not evaluate technological development
as inherently positive or negative.

Its central concern is the structural relationship between
two dimensions:

1. Complexity of autonomous systems.
2. Human interpretive capacity.

## Core Theoretical Concepts

### Structural Complexity

- Architectural layering.
- Decision dimensions.
- Emergent behavioural patterns.
- Network integration.
- Operational transparency.

### Human Interpretive Capacity

- Operational mental models.
- Recognition of system limitations.
- Bounded predictive orientation.
- Responsibility structures.
- Human interpretive oversight.

## Structural Implications

A persistent imbalance may be associated with:

- Delegated decision-making.
- Intermediary interpretive layers.
- Reduced direct transparency.
- Diffusion of responsibility.

These are theoretical implications, not empirically established
causal relationships.

## Analytical Scales

CIR can be examined at:

- Individual scale.
- Institutional scale.
- Civilizational scale.

## Theoretical Position

CIR is intended to be:

- Non-normative.
- Scale-independent.
- Time-independent.
- Platform-independent.
- Conceptually relational.

## Research Limitations

Version 1 does not contain:

- A validated mathematical formula.
- An empirical measurement instrument.
- A validated numerical threshold.
- Empirical datasets.
- Demonstrated predictive capabilities.
- Formal peer-review validation.

It should be described as a foundational theoretical framework.
